name: Vitruvius
summary: Author of De architectura (c.30-15 BCE), the only major Roman work on architecture to survive. Defined firmitas, utilitas, venustas — the canonical triad of architectural quality.

name: Ebenezer Howard
summary: Founder of the Garden City movement. To-morrow: A Peaceful Path to Real Reform (1898), republished as Garden Cities of To-morrow (1902). Inspired Letchworth and Welwyn.

name: Clarence Perry
summary: Defined the Neighborhood Unit (1929) — a residential cell sized to a primary school's catchment, with arterials at the perimeter and a community focus at the center.
sources: The Neighborhood Unit, Regional Plan of NY, 1929

name: Le Corbusier
summary: Author of Vers une architecture (1923) and the Modulor. Co-founder of CIAM (1928). Defined the Five Points of New Architecture and the Radiant City.

name: Jane Jacobs
summary: Author of The Death and Life of Great American Cities (1961). Articulated four conditions for urban diversity: mixed primary uses, short blocks, mixed-age buildings, sufficient density. Coined eyes on the street.
sources: The Death and Life of Great American Cities, 1961

name: Kevin Lynch
summary: MIT planner and theorist of cognitive cities. The Image of the City (1960) defined five elements of urban legibility: paths, edges, districts, nodes, landmarks.

name: Christopher Alexander
summary: Berkeley architect-mathematician. A Pattern Language (1977) catalogued 253 patterns from region to construction detail. Later work: The Nature of Order (2002-04).

name: Jan Gehl
summary: Author of Life Between Buildings (1971) and Cities for People (2010). Defined the 12 Quality Criteria for public space. Transformed Copenhagen, Melbourne, NYC street life.

name: Gordon Cullen
summary: The Concise Townscape (1961). Coined serial vision — the cumulative experience of urban space as a sequence of revealed views.

name: Camillo Sitte
summary: City Planning According to Artistic Principles (1889). Defined plaza proportions and enclosure rules grounded in Renaissance and medieval Italian precedent.
sources: Der Städtebau nach seinen künstlerischen Grundsätzen, 1889

name: Andres Duany
summary: Co-founder of Duany Plater-Zyberk (DPZ) and the Congress for the New Urbanism (CNU). Author of the SmartCode and the Transect (T1-T6) framework.
sources: The Lexicon of the New Urbanism

name: Leon Krier
summary: Architect-theorist of the polycentric city. Architecture: Choice or Fate (1998), The Architecture of Community (2009). Master-planner of Poundbury.

name: Ian Bentley
summary: Lead author of Responsive Environments (1985). Defined seven qualities of responsive design: permeability, variety, legibility, robustness, visual appropriateness, richness, personalisation.

name: Bill Hillier
summary: Founder of Space Syntax at UCL. The Social Logic of Space (1984), Space is the Machine (1996). Mathematicised street network configuration via integration and choice.

name: Carlos Moreno
summary: Sorbonne professor; coined the 15-Minute City (2016). Mayor Hidalgo's Paris program built on his framework.

name: Timothy Beatley
summary: UVA professor. Coined Biophilic Cities (2010). Founder of the Biophilic Cities Network.

name: Frei Otto
summary: Pioneer of form-finding and lightweight tensile structures. Munich Olympic Park (1972). Founded IL Stuttgart. Pritzker laureate 2015.

name: Patrik Schumacher
summary: Director of Zaha Hadid Architects. Author of Parametricism — A New Global Style for Architecture and Urban Design (2008) and The Autopoiesis of Architecture (2010-12).

name: Achim Menges
summary: Founder of ICD Stuttgart. Pioneer of material computation, robotic fabrication, and integrative design — fibre-composite pavilions and timber Landesgartenschau structures.

name: Neri Oxman
summary: Founder of MIT Mediated Matter (2010-2020). Material Ecology — coupling biology, computation, and fabrication. Silk Pavilion, Aguahoja, Glass.

name: Philippe Block
summary: ETH Zurich professor; co-director of NCCR Digital Fabrication. Thrust Network Analysis for compression-only shells. Armadillo Vault (2016), HiLo roof.

name: Greg Lynn
summary: Animate Form (1999). Brought blob architecture and time-based computational form to architectural discourse in the 1990s.
